articles.title: IMCWP 24 Contribution of CP Mexico (PCM)
articles.author: MLToday
articles.content: Comrades, We thank the Central Committee of the Communist Party of Cuba for organizing this IMCWP —the 24th since this initiative began [in 1998] as part of the 150th anniversary of the Communist Manifesto, at the call of the Communist Party of Greece—despite the very difficult conditions. This forum has now been in existence for more than a quarter of a century and has become a fundamental platform for the exchange of opinions and information under the new conditions in which the international communist movement has had to operate, after the predominance of market relations—incompatible with socialist construction—led to the temporary triumph of the counterrevolution in the USSR and other countries.. We have come to pay tribute to Commander Fidel Castro Ruz on the occasion of the centenary of his birth. From a very young age he chose the path of revolution and internationalism, convinced that it represented the emancipation and happiness of the people and workers of Cuba, and the liberation of Cuba from the dreadful chains of imperialism. The popular uprising against the dictatorship of Batista – which was supported by legal and illegal capital, the White House,and the mafia in holy alliance – linked the longed-for independence with socialism, at the time of the historical transition from capitalism to socialism inaugurated by the Great October Socialist Revolution of 1917, of the general laws of revolution, which does not specify an intermediate stage between socialism and capitalism, as Commander Ernesto Guevara summarizes in his maxim, “either socialist revolution or a parody of revolution.” In fact, in addition to facing the Cuban bourgeoisie, the US monopolies, and imperialism, the Cuban Revolution and the thought and action of Commander Fidel Castro also brought about a questioning of the opportunistic line of Browderism and its offshoots, such as class collaboration and reformism within the communist movement on our continent, and also in Cuba. While some petty-bourgeois currents, capitalizing on the prestige of the Cuban Revolution, sought to deny the indispensable role of the Communist Party in the revolutionary process—and even the historical revolutionary character of the working class—Fidel fought with determination to bring the various revolutionary forces together into a new Communist Party of Cuba. This party was the continuation of the one founded by Carlos Baliño and Julio Antonio Mella as the Cuban section of the Third International, and by placing the proletariat at the helm of the Revolution at all levels, making it clear—as the Comandante[1] explained on several occasions—that there would never again be power of the bourgeoisie, by the bourgeoisie, and for the bourgeoisie, but rather power of the workers, by the workers, and for the workers. Fidel earned the respect of the international communist and revolutionary movement, and his prestige grew even further when, in the face of the temporary setback of socialist construction in the USSR and Eastern Europe—and against all odds—he steadfastly maintained the socialist direction of the Cuban revolutionary process in order to preserve the socialist gains and guarantee the right to continue socialist construction in the future. We have much to learn from Fidel, especially in his thought and action. We also come here to reiterate our solidarity with the people of Cuba and with the socialist achievements of the Revolution. The arrival of the U.S. fleet in the Caribbean and the Trump administration’s proclamation of the new U.S. National Security Doctrine show us that the fierce competition between the capitalist economies led by the U.S. and the EU and the so-called multipolar economies—with their conflicts and wars—also involves Latin America. The confessed goal of the US in its new doctrine is to drive Chinese capital out of the region to regain its hegemony. That policy of aggression immediately turned to action, and after the attack on Venezuela -which had the heroic resistance of 32 Cuban fighters- and the imposition of an ad hoc government, Trump focused his aim against Cuba. Since then, week after week, measures are incessantly adopted to suffocate Cuba, the main thrust being the imposition of a total energy blockade against the people of Cuba, which reinforces and sharpens the economic blockade that is already 64 years old. Threatening with sanctions and tariffs the US has managed to get several States to yield to the pressures, giving up their own sovereignty to trade with third countries freely. They have tried to bend the revolution, sanctioning cadres and organizations, attacking with surgical precision the inflow of productive and financial inputs, but they have met with the wall of a people resolved to defend the chosen path. They have even had the cynicism and cowardice to personally attack General Raúl Castro. The Cuban Revolution from its first steps in power faced hostility, economic warfare and even direct military aggression, but in recent years, this new aggressive wave is the most serious. And the response of the peoples, of international solidarity and of the communist parties, must be up to the circumstances, both politically and concretely. For example, the people of Mexico, with the labor movement and the communists as its backbone, conquered sovereignty over that energy resource with the oil expropriation of 1938. Unfortunately the Mexican State recently gave in to US pressures and suspended the oil agreements with Cuba. In response to this, the people-to-people campaign of “An oil ship for Cuba”, to which the PCM contributes with its activity, together with other organizations of Mexico, and with the fraternal co-operation of sister parties such as the PCTE [Communist Party of the Workers of Spain], acquires relevance. We consider solidarity with Cuba and the defense of its socialist achievements an imperative at this time. There are countless initiatives of the PCM and the Communist Youth, in workplaces, people’s neighborhoods, schools, in favor of Cuba and against imperialist aggression. Along with the campaign against Cuba and the war of aggression against the people of Iran, Palestine and Lebanon, it is also notorious that the Trump Administration is promoting a campaign against socialism and communism. The ruling classes always keep in mind who their class enemy is. It is true that the ideological mechanisms of imperialism distort history and facts, and they manipulate. For example, they present socialism as what it is not, such as the progressive management of capitalism, or the American democratic socialists, and even the US Democratic Party itself. However, it is clear that, in the face of these distortions and attacks, we communists have a duty to defend our theory—Marxism-Leninism—and our historical goals: socialism-communism, socialist construction in the USSR, and the characteristics of socialism, such as the socialization of the means of production, the central and scientific planning of the economy, revolutionary workers’ power, and the dictatorship of the proletariat. Historical experience has shown us the superiority of the new mode of production of socialism-communism in satisfying the people’s needs, in bringing about happiness and progress, and in unleashing the full potential and creativity of humanity once the system of exploitation is abolished. It also showed us the suffering our peoples endure when setbacks occur, when the counterrevolution gains ground, for socialist construction is not an upward trajectory without a life-and-death struggle against commodity-money relations—which are the seed of capitalism— upon which the possibility of a temporary setback is objectively based, since accumulation and profit give rise to the petty bourgeoisie and the bourgeoisie—the remnants of the overthrown exploiting classes, mortal enemies of the socialist revolution and of workers’ and people’s power. Let us always bear that bitter lesson in mind. We face difficult times, with an unfavorable correlation [of forces], but, with struggle, we can change that. Difficult times must not overshadow the historical optimism based on Marxism-Leninism, of the coming of new socialist revolutions. The objective conditions show us the imperialist war and the acute inter-imperialist competition; the shocks of the capitalist economic crisis; the superprofits of monopolies and the impoverishment of the working class; the devastation of natural resources and the environment; the tragic results of facing global pandemics under capitalist management; the attacks on working women and migrant workers; the open genocide of a people seen by the world; the galloping development of new productive forces, such as Artificial Intelligence, subordinated to the logic of capital accumulation. But in the face of all these dangers and attacks, a class capable of transforming this situation is rising up and resisting—a class that is fighting and organizing all over the world. And from all this, there is only one conclusion: Let us strengthen the struggle for socialism-communism, for new socialist revolutions. Cuba will win! Long live Fidel! _______________________________________________________________ [1] For example in his speech at the Cuba Vive International Youth Festival on August 6, 1995. articles.title: IMCWP 24: Contribution of the CP of the Workers of Spain
articles.author: MLToday
articles.content: Havana, August 2026 The Communist Party of the Workers of Spain thanks the organisers for convening this meeting and extends fraternal greetings to all the participating organisations and, most especially, to the Communist Party of Cuba, the Cuban people, and all the individuals and organisations that keep solidarity with the Cuban Revolution alive. The commemoration of the centenary of Fidel Castro’s birth is an occasion of particular importance to recall his life and work, assess the historical significance of the Cuban Revolution, and renew our commitment to solidarity with Cuba. Fidel is part of the contemporary history of Cuba, Latin America, and the international communist and revolutionary movement. His figure is synonymous with an entire life devoted to socialism-communism and to the defense of workers’ and popular interests. The Cuban Revolution opened a new stage in the history of the island. It made it possible to advance in building a social model that placed the needs of the majority of the population at its center and turned fundamental rights into pillars of collective life. The achievements made in areas such as education, healthcare, science, culture, and social protection are an international benchmark. Cuba has shown that, even under extraordinarily difficult conditions, it is possible to devote a country’s resources and capabilities to improving the living conditions of its people. The expansion of education, the eradication of illiteracy, full equality between women and men, the development of a universal healthcare system, scientific training, and the promotion of culture form part of a legacy that must be known, defended, and carried forward into the future. These achievements have also had to be developed under the effects of a sustained policy of economic, commercial, and financial blockade imposed by the United States for more than six decades. The blockade directly affects the daily lives of the Cuban population. It hinders access to medicines, food, energy, technology, financing, and other essential resources. Its extraterritorial nature extends its effects far beyond relations between Cuba and the United States. Every country in the world is subjected to pressure and sanctions for maintaining normal relations with the island. For this reason, the PCTE reiterates its demand for the immediate and unconditional lifting of the blockade. It is an unjust policy, prolonged for decades and directed against the living conditions of the Cuban people. Opposition to the blockade must occupy a central place in solidarity work. Expressing sympathy for Cuba is not enough. It is necessary to explain the concrete consequences of this policy, combat disinformation, and promote initiatives capable of broadening social support for the Cuban people. The Communist and Workers’ Parties present at this meeting share a common responsibility. We must improve coordination, ensure continuity in our campaigns, exchange experiences, and develop joint actions that enable solidarity to reach broader sections of the working class and the people in our respective countries. Solidarity must be active, organised, and constant. It must be expressed through the political denunciation of the blockade, but also through material, cultural, educational, scientific, and social cooperation. It must foster a rigorous understanding of Cuban reality and combat campaigns that seek to reduce the complexity of the country’s situation to self-serving explanations. Spain and Cuba are united by deep historical, cultural, and human ties. These ties provide an important basis for strengthening relations between our two peoples and developing initiatives of cooperation and solidarity. We consider it necessary for Spanish institutions to maintain a clear and firm position against the blockade and to contribute to the development of normal relations with Cuba in all fields. They must also act to prevent coercive measures imposed by the United States from conditioning Cuba’s relations with European countries. Fidel’s legacy also possesses a fundamental internationalist dimension. For decades, Cuba has carried out extensive cooperation with numerous countries, particularly in the fields of healthcare, education, and science. Thousands of Cuban professionals have worked in places affected by epidemics, natural disasters, armed conflicts, or severe social deprivation. Cuban medical cooperation has made it possible to care for millions of people who lacked access to healthcare services. Literacy programmes, the training of foreign students, and participation in development projects have turned solidarity into a concrete practice. Cuba has not merely offered what it had left over. It has shared its knowledge, resources, and the efforts of its professionals even at times of great internal difficulty. This example takes on particular importance in a world marked by growing inequality, economic competition, the proliferation of conflicts, and rising military expenditure. Against a conception of international relations based on imposition and the pursuit of profit, Cuba has defended cooperation, mutual assistance, and shared responsibility in addressing humanity’s major problems. The Cuban experience demonstrates that internationalism is not an abstraction. It is expressed through doctors, teachers, scientists, and workers who place their abilities at the service of other peoples. Honouring Fidel’s legacy means preserving and strengthening this conception of solidarity; it also means defending peace and opposing imperialist aggression. Peace cannot be understood merely as the temporary absence of war. It requires combating the conditions that generate violence, inequality, exploitation, and conflict among peoples. It requires rejecting policies of pressure, economic sanctions, military threats, and any form of intervention intended to impose the interests of the great powers. In the current international context, characterised by intensifying rivalries among powers and the danger of new conflicts, it is essential to strengthen the common action of communist, workers’, and popular organisations. We must join forces against militarism, the arms race, and the use of peoples as instruments in disputes among powers. At the same time, we must maintain a clear position against the idea that changes in the international balance of forces will, by themselves, lead to a more just world. Lasting peace cannot be built upon competition among major economic interests, but upon cooperation, equality, and the fulfilment of popular needs. The centenary of Fidel’s birth must not become a purely ceremonial occasion. Fidel was a revolutionary leader who defended the capacity of peoples to transform society in a revolutionary direction, the importance of political organisation, and the need to remain steadfast even in the most adverse circumstances. Honouring his legacy means studying his thought and practice but also applying his lessons to the problems of our time. It means trusting in the strength of the people, understanding that great social achievements are not concessions but the result of organisation and struggle, and defending socialism-communism as the necessary and urgent alternative to capitalism, which produces nothing but inequality, crisis, exploitation, and war. The Cuban experience demonstrates that the principal social achievements of its people have been made possible by socialist construction, social ownership of the fundamental resources, and the orientation of the economy towards satisfying collective needs. Preserving and strengthening these foundations is the best guarantee for defending the rights already won and continuing to advance in the face of the difficulties of the present. The Communist Party of the Workers of Spain reaffirms its commitment to the Cuban Revolution, to denouncing the blockade, and to developing ever closer relations between our peoples. We also express our willingness to continue working with Communist and Workers’ Parties and solidarity forces throughout the world to promote common initiatives. The centenary of Fidel’s birth must serve to renew our commitments: our commitment to the memory and legacy of the Cuban Revolution; to the struggle for the lifting of the blockade; to internationalist solidarity; and to peace and opposition to imperialist aggression. It must also renew our commitment to socialism as a historical project capable of placing the economy, labour, and knowledge at the service of human needs. From Spain, we convey to the Cuban people our respect, recognition, and solidarity. We will continue working to strengthen joint actions, broaden the solidarity movement, and defend Cuba’s achievements and socialist future. articles.title: IMCWP 24: Contribution of the CP Canada
articles.author: MLToday
articles.content: The contribution of the Communist Party of Canada to the 24th International Meeting of Communist and Workers’ Parties (IMCWP) held in Havana from August 7 to 8, 2026. On behalf of the Central Executive Committee of the Communist Party of Canada, I bring fraternal greetings to the 24th International Meeting of Communist and Workers’ Parties. We thank the Communist Party of Cuba for hosting this important gathering in Havana. We salute the heroic Cuban people and their socialist revolution, which for over six decades has stood as a beacon of dignity, resistance and proletarian internationalism in the face of the most brutal imperialist siege. The Communist Party of Canada vehemently condemns the ongoing United States blockade against Cuba, an act of collective punishment and economic warfare that flagrantly violates the UN Charter and international law. Shamefully, the Mark Carney government in Canada has begun shifting Canada’s longstanding positions regarding Cuba. In July, Canada abstained when the majority of the world voted to debate the U.S.’s inhumane and genocidal actions. Prime Minister Carney postures about Canadian sovereignty, yet his government has deepened Cuba’s isolation by issuing travel warnings that suspended all flights from Canada, disrupting Cuba’s tourism industry. The Canadian government has channelled token aid to NGOs instead of the Cuban government, and Canada has maintained silence in the face of threats of invasion and while the blockade attempts to strangle the Cuban people. We say: no more appeasement of Trump and Rubio. We demand that the Canadian government immediately break its complicity with the blockade and denounce it, lift the travel advisory, and send oil to Cuba. Comrades, we meet at a moment of profound danger. The growing capitalist crisis of overaccumulation and the rise of new centres of economic power, such as Russia, India and China, have led the most aggressive imperialist forces, above all United States imperialism, to abandon even the pretense of multilateralism. While the decline of US imperialism is relative, it remains the main imperialist threat. We are witnessing a return to naked barbarism, where US imperialism uses tariffs, sanctions, and now openly uses military force to maintain hegemony. These methods are not anomalies of capitalism but are an inherent part of the imperialist stage’s drive towards war. The US attack on Venezuela and Iran are flagrant violations of the UN Charter. With the full support of US imperialism, the fascist, Zionist government of Netanyahu has drastically deepened its genocide of the Palestinians in Gaza and the West Bank. These increased aggressions and massive militarization are an existential threat to humankind in the form of the growing threat of nuclear war and accelerating climate catastrophe. Anger over declining wages and living standards are leading the bourgeoisie to promote rising reactionary and fascist movements that pretend to be anti-system. In an increasing number of countries, right-wing populism now holds state power. As Dimitrov taught us, the victory of fascism attests to the weakness of the working class, disorganized by class collaboration, and the weakness of bourgeois rule through the old methods. We see our task as not to form alliances with more “democratic” bourgeois forces that advocate continued erosion of living standards, but to build the anti-monopoly, anti-imperialist alliance of the working class and its allies that can be a genuine barrier to fascism by undermining the objective conditions that allow fascist movements to grow. We must fight the growing reaction with an independent, class-struggle alternative that offers working people advances, not on the basis of an imagined return to a failed liberal normalcy. Comrades, Canada is an imperialist country in its own right, closely allied with U.S. capital. Behind the rhetoric, Carney’s goal, and that of Canada’s monopolies, is to further integrate and subordinate Canada’s economy to the United States, despite current disputes with Trump. We reject the false choice between reactionary protectionism and corporate free trade; both serve capital at the expense of working people. We fight for multilateral and mutually beneficial trade deals in the spirit of the inspiring example of ALBA. The Carney government talks about sovereignty against Trump’s threats to Canada itself or to Greenland, but continues to tail US imperialism. Carney’s response is not to resist imperialism but to reorient itself within it. His “middle powers” project is a plan for Canadian and European imperialism to get a seat at the head of the table, not to get rid of the table. Carney’s outreach to Europe, including joining the European defence procurement program, demonstrates rising interimperialist rivalry. Yet there has been no major rupture in the US-NATO camp. Marco Rubio’s speech in Munich early this year, in which he praised European colonialism and railed against communism, was welcomed by European elites. Despite tactical disagreements, the transatlantic imperialist alliance, including Canada, remains intact, united by its shared position atop the global system of capitalist exploitation. The increased aggression of imperialism is tearing apart international law and the United Nations’ Charter. We fully understand the UN’s limitations. Imperialism scorns international law unless compelled by a stronger balance of class forces. However, the UN Charter itself emerged from the 1945 victory over fascism, when socialist forces were advancing in a united bloc. The fact that the United States and Israel are increasingly attacking these institutions proves that the UN remains an obstacle to their aggression. Our Party defends the principles of international law: sovereign equality, self-determination, non-intervention, and peaceful resolution of disputes. The task is to defend these principles and struggle to democratize the UN into a body that serves the peoples of the world. Comrades, the struggle inside Canada is sharpening as well. The Carney government uses US annexation and tariff threats as pretext for the deepest austerity since the 1990s. While claiming to defend sovereignty, Carney dismantles social programs and has promised to eliminate 40,000 public service jobs, while threatening to turn remaining public servants into army reservists. More layoffs will follow in the private sector. His plan to triple military spending to 5% of GDP by 2035 can only be financed by slashing health, education, and social services. Carney’s military stimulus is justified by claims it will create jobs, but this is a lie designed to funnel public money to monopoly corporate interests. The research proves otherwise: For every $1 million spent on the military, only 5 jobs are created. The same amount on healthcare creates 9 jobs, and on education, 13 jobs. War spending is the least effective way to put food on working families’ tables and the most effective way to move public funds to corporate profits. What unites all major federal parties in Canada today, is their commitment to capitalism. Not one advocates leaving NATO or opposes a significant expansion of militarization. With little to no working-class representation in Parliament, the struggle in Canada is largely extra-parliamentary. The real alternative to the corporate agenda of war and austerity is a working-class, anti-monopoly, anti-imperialist people’s coalition. A coalition in the streets with a reflection in electoral politics that demands the nationalization of energy and natural resources and key industries like auto, steel, shipbuilding and aerospace under democratic control, to guarantee jobs and production for social needs. A coalition that fights for a full-employment economy, funded by cutting the war budget and taxing corporations and the rich. A program that builds two million units of social housing to end the housing crisis. Our task in this volatile and dangerous period is to bring this program to the working class and build the movement capable of winning it. This anti-monopoly, anti-imperialist alliance we seek cannot be composed only of communists, but it cannot exist without communists organized independently as its foundation. The alliance would not necessarily lead to socialism; however, given Canada’s objective and subjective conditions, forging such an alliance rooted in labour and democratic struggles corresponds to the current phase of the struggle to gather forces to overthrow capitalism. Comrades, we are thankful that the International Meeting of Communist and Workers’ Parties has convened after a gap of two years. Comradely, principled discussions among the parties with the aim of clarifying and deepening our political analysis are very important and have been missed in the last two years. But, most important is united action on core questions: in full solidarity with Cuba and Palestine, opposition to militarization and imperialist war, and the fight for labour and democratic rights in the face of rising war and reaction. Our meetings are far more than symbolic exercises. Internationalism is one of our greatest strengths and we need to build upon it to strengthen our movement, for never have we seen a world where socialism is more necessary. We express our confidence in the unity of Communist and Workers’ parties in our historic struggle against oppression and exploitation and for peace and socialism. Long live socialist Cuba! Long live Marxism-Leninism! Long live proletarian internationalism! The post IMCWP 24: Contribution of the CP Canada appeared first on MLToday .

articles.title: IMCWP 24: Contribution of the German Communist Party (DKP)
articles.author: MLToday
articles.content: Contribution of the German Communist Party (DKP) The Cuban people and the Communist Party of Cuba are waging a heroic struggle against imperialism’s murderous blockade. They wage it for humanity, for humanity’s future, for socialism. To hold our international meeting under these conditions deserves gratitude and places on us the responsibility to do everything for Cuba’s victory, for its people, for the defense of socialism. Cuba will win! Imperialism, having been forced onto the defensive, is trying to preserve its hegemony by violent means — economic, political, or military. This includes the war against Russia through Ukraine, which also aims at confrontation with socialist China, whose development of the productive forces now appears impossible to catch up with. It includes the enforcement of imperialist interests in West Asia through the genocide of the Palestinian people and the war of aggression against Iran and Lebanon. And it includes the attempt to destroy socialism in Cuba. To this end, Cuba has been declared a special threat — a threat that plainly consists in the fact that Cuban society, its free healthcare and education system, its socialist development, and its resistance to imperialist threats stand as a model for other peoples: a model of pursuing a sovereign path of development oriented to the interests of working people. Cuba thereby plays an important role not only in the struggles in Latin America but in struggles across the whole world, including in the imperialist countries — including here in the Federal Republic of Germany. Cuba does not stand alone in this struggle. The counterforces against US-led imperialism are growing stronger. This concerns the growing economic strength of the People’s Republic of China and its global projects such as the Belt and Road initiative, and progress toward a multipolar world order that allows many countries at least partial release from dependency on imperialism. The struggle against neocolonial dependency is intensifying. Of great importance in this process is the cooperation between the People’s Republic of China and the Russian Federation, as well as the BRICS grouping. But solidarity from within the imperialist countries is also of great importance — most recently visible in the “Nuestra America Convoy” action and the international brigade for May 1st. Solidarity with countries threatened by imperialism — Cuba foremost among them — therefore plays a major role in our party’s struggle. We are proud that a solidarity brigade of the SDAJ, our youth organization, with nearly 30 young people from Germany, is in Cuba right now. The anti-imperialist struggle must be waged in all countries simultaneously and jointly. This solidarity cannot therefore be separated from the struggle against German imperialism’s war policy — these are two sides of the same coin. German imperialism, despite existing and growing conflicts, still subordinates itself to US imperialism. This was also evident in Germany’s vote at the UN General Assembly in July 2026 on Cuba’s blockade. A very large majority condemned the blockade; Germany was among those that abstained. Foreign Minister Wadephul had previously declared that he “does not see a blockade.” German imperialism has, however, by no means abandoned its ambitions for world-power status; to pursue them it needs NATO, and it also needs the EU, which at Germany’s urging is becoming increasingly militarized. It is therefore in German imperialism’s interest to rearm NATO and the EU and to fully subordinate Ukraine — as part of Eastern Europe — to imperialist policy. In West Asia too, German imperialism stands at the forefront of imperialist aggression, through its unconditional support for Israel and its refusal to recognize the war of aggression against Iran as a violation of international law. This imperialist war policy and the extreme rearmament come at the expense of working people, including in the imperialist countries themselves. In Germany, with the approval of all parties in the Bundestag — with the partial exception of members of “Die Linke” — social rights are being dismantled, from pensions to working-time regulations to healthcare and education. A reintroduction of conscription is planned. Infrastructure is increasingly being aligned with military purposes. The state is responding to the possible growth of protest with a marked rollback of democratic rights. This includes the criminal prosecution of Palestine solidarity activists and of those who publicly point to NATO’s responsibility for the war in Ukraine, the banning of Soviet flags at demonstrations, police assaults, and the persecution of young activists in the school strike movement against conscription. Meanwhile, protest is growing — though by no means to a sufficient degree — as more and more people notice that their living conditions are steadily worsening, and push back. There are now also more openings for this within the trade unions, still largely dominated by the Social Democratic Party and bound into imperialist politics. We see our central task at present as strengthening these openings within the unions, achieving a break of the unions’ integration into the politics of imperialism, bringing about cooperation between the workers’ movement and the peace movement, and at the same time carrying a consistent anti-NATO course into this struggle. Let us stress once again: this struggle against imperialist war policy cannot be separated from international solidarity. In our country, in the coming weeks, solidarity actions with socialist Cuba will take place — against the genocidal blockade, against the military threats of US imperialism. Our party, too, will continue its actions in support of socialist Cuba and its Communist Party. Cuba is resisting, and Cuba will win! Socialism will win! articles.title: IMCWP 24: Contribution of the Palestinian CP
articles.author: MLToday
articles.content: Contribution of the Palestinian Communist Party at the 24th International Meeting of Communist and Workers’ Parties in the Cuban Capital, Havana Comrades, General Secretary of the Communist Party of Cuba, leaders and representatives of the Communist and Workers’ Parties, honorable attendees, On behalf of the Palestinian Communist Party, the party of the Palestinian working class, we extend to you our highest militant greetings. We hope that this 24th International Meeting will be crowned with success in its struggle to unite the ranks of our communist movement in the face of the fierce imperialist assault on our peoples. We also extend a special tribute of reverence and admiration to the revolutionary people of Cuba and their Communist Party. We meet today on the land of the steadfast Cuban Revolution, which faces the largest imperialist attacks and the unjust economic and financial blockade since the Bay of Pigs invasion. This meeting convenes in conjunction with the centenary of the birth of the father of the Cuban Revolution, the immortal Comrade Fidel Castro, and takes place in close proximity to the dens of colonialism, where the free Cuban people built socialism and proved to the world that peoples are capable of victory. We reaffirm our full solidarity with Cuba and demand its definitive removal from any unilateral lists of state sponsors of terrorism. Comrades, Our meeting convenes under highly complex international circumstances witnessing a dangerous acceleration in global transformations. Global capitalism, in its imperialist stage, is experiencing a deep structural crisis—an intractable crisis of overproduction. Historically, capitalism has resolved its contradictions and crises by igniting wars, whether major ones like the First and Second World Wars, or smaller wars in Vietnam, Korea, Iraq, Afghanistan, and finally in Iran. Today, this acute imperialist struggle over raw materials, markets, trade routes, and energy is escalating. The capitalist powers, led by US imperialism and its allies, are resorting to militarization and fueling chauvinistic tendencies, the far-right, racist regimes, and fascism when bourgeois democracy fails to contain these crises. The principled Marxist-Leninist position asserts that inter-capitalist wars always aim to control sources of wealth. Hence, it is our party’s view that the Russian-Ukrainian war is an expression of the crisis and contradictions of the global capitalist system, and of the struggle among imperialist powers for influence, interests, and strategic positions. This war cannot be understood in isolation from NATO’s military expansionist policies and US hegemony following the coup against socialism in the Soviet Union. At the same time, Russia’s use of military force or the violation of Ukraine’s sovereignty cannot be justified; Russia today is a capitalist state governed by class and geopolitical interests, not a socialist alternative to Western hegemony. The principled stance of the communist and workers’ forces is based on the rejection of imperialist wars in all their forms, and the refusal to turn peoples into fuel for the conflicts of major powers. The primary victims of this war are the workers, the toiling masses, and the peoples, while arms corporations and major monopolies reap the benefits. Therefore, the solution lies in stopping the war, resorting to a political solution that guarantees the rights and sovereignty of peoples, and struggling for a more just international order based on peace and cooperation among peoples, far from military hegemony and polarization. Dear Comrades, The capitalist and imperialist assault on peoples has shown its most hideous fascist face in our region through the alliance of fascist Zionism and religious extremism. The war on the Gaza Strip has turned into one of the most horrific crimes of genocide, ethnic cleansing, and systematic starvation in the modern era, aimed at breaking the will of our people and uprooting them from their land. Simultaneously, the West Bank, including occupied Jerusalem, faces the fiercest forms of apartheid and rabid settlement expansion. The West Bank has been fragmented by more than 1,300 electronic gates and military checkpoints, transformed into isolated enclaves and cantons to end the historical national existence of our people. This criminal Zionist assault has not been limited to the land of Palestine; it has extended to sisterly Lebanon and its resisting people through brutal aggression, targeting residential areas and civilians, and violating its national sovereignty in a blatant Zionist-imperialist attempt to expand the scope of the war and subjugate the resistance forces in the region. We declare from this podium our firm internationalist solidarity with the brotherly Lebanese people and their valiant resistance in confronting this brutal Zionist aggression. In this same context, the repeated US-Zionist aggressions and threats against Iran and its sovereignty are seen as an integral part of the imperialist strategy to subjugate the entire region and dismantle any axis that disrupts the absolute hegemony of US imperialism and its Zionist ally over energy sources and strategic corridors. We view this aggression as an attempt to impose new colonial equations through armed force and suffocating economic sanctions. We reaffirm our principled position upholding the absolute right of peoples to protect their sovereignty and national independence in the face of imperialist plots that seek to ignite a comprehensive regional war serving only the interests of the military-industrial complex and monopoly capital networks. Dear Comrades, “Our party, the Palestinian Communist Party, engages with all its capabilities and cadres on the front lines to confront this fascist Zionist assault. In the Gaza Strip, the party makes immense sacrifices, offering blood as a group of our comrades ascended as martyrs in the battle of confronting the occupation. In the West Bank, our comrades are subjected to continuous arrests and persecution. Under these complex conditions, our party continues its struggle in all forms to restore our legitimate national rights. It focuses its tireless efforts on the ground to form a broad national front that unites the living forces hostile to the occupation and to the liquidationist ‘Oslo’ approach—a front whose features are gradually taking shape today, despite all the restrictions and persecutions by the Palestinian Authority apparatuses that are complicit with the occupation, targeting our party and the struggling national forces.” Comrades, The struggle of the Palestinian people is not merely a local political conflict; it is an inherent part and an advanced front of the internationalist struggle against imperialism, colonialism, and plunder. Therefore, we emphasize before this podium the utmost importance of the role of the global communist movement. Imperialism operates as an internationally interconnected bloc, and confronting it requires a unified internationalist response and struggle based on the unity of the working class and oppressed peoples. History has proven that the unity of the communist movement has always been the safety valve and the primary pillar for victory over fascism and colonialism, and that the decline of this coordination gives enemies the space to impose their projects. Thus, we call for developing more effective forms of coordination, organizing comprehensive solidarity and boycott campaigns against the occupation, collectively standing against blockades, sanctions, and imperialist military alliances, and rebuilding the global socialist project on revolutionary Marxist-Leninist foundations. Hence, our party reaffirms before you, comrades, its proposition and unwavering historical position: The Palestinian Communist Party’s vision and just solution for the Palestinian cause does not lie within the 1967 borders. Rather, we reject this partition and emphasize our principled goal of completely ending the Zionist settler-colonial project, and establishing a single democratic state over the entire Palestinian territory—a state for all its sons and daughters, where all components live on the basis of full equality in rights and duties without any national, religious, or ethnic discrimination; a state that guarantees the sacred right of return for Palestinian refugees to their homes in accordance with UN Resolution 194, paving the way towards socialism and social justice. In conclusion, we extend our deepest thanks and appreciation to the Communist Party of Cuba for their warm reception and for hosting this important meeting. We renew our faith that the banner of workers’ internationalism will remain flying high, and that free peoples are capable of defeating occupation, fascism, and imperialism, and building a new world dominated by peace and socialism. Glory to the struggling peoples. Glory to internationalist solidarity. Freedom for all of Palestine, from the river to the sea. Long live the Communist International. articles.title: Somalia on the Brink of Mass Starvation: A Vortex of Climate Shocks, War and Aid Cuts
articles.author: MLToday
articles.content: Somalia is already reeling from repeated droughts and floods, with millions facing acute hunger. Now economic shocks from the war on Iran compound US cuts to humanitarian aid, as El Niño’s peak portends devastating floods once again. By Pavan Kulkarni September 8, 2026 Breakthrough News Somali women displaced by drought sit at Feynuus Nutrition Centre on the outskirts of the capital, Mogadishu, Somalia Wednesday, Aug. 19, 2026. Photo: AP With floods forecast to follow on the heels of a prolonged drought amid rising malnutrition and displacement, “Somalia is right on the cusp of something much worse,” Jeremy Konyndyk, president of Refugees International, said on September 3. Following a fact-finding visit to the East African country, ranked 123rd among the 123 countries in the 2025 Global Hunger Index, Konyndyk said, “Families have exhausted nearly every coping mechanism at their disposal.” They had already endured the worst drought in 40 years that parched the Horn of Africa since 2020. The end of the drought in 2023 brought no relief because when it finally rained, it was a deluge – washing away crops and livestock that had survived the drought. A locust outbreak left behind by the floods destroyed more crops. “Somalia is at the epicenter of climate change, despite its negligible greenhouse gas emissions, and suffers recurrent extreme weather events that destroy lives and livelihoods,” the World Food Program (WFP) explains . Families had barely recovered from these shocks when the Somali government declared yet another drought emergency in November 2025.
